_comment: Committable .claude/settings.json for an L9 consumer repo. Copy to .claude/settings.json
and commit it: on Claude Code Web/Mobile only git-tracked files survive the clone, so a
committed settings.json is what makes governance boot with no manual step. On the CLI the
same file is picked up locally. Keep secrets OUT of this file — they belong in the account
environment (web/environment.env.example) or user-scope config, never in a repo.
Field/event names track the Claude Code release; see https://code.claude.com/docs.
permissions.allow lets the bounded-autonomy runtime complete work end to end: scoped git
writes (branch/worktree/commit), CI inspection (gh run/pr checks), read-only GitHub
queries, PR monitoring (subscribe/unsubscribe), and `make pr` — so completed work
opens a PR and is driven to green via the l9-pr-remediation loop WITHOUT a prompt.
PUBLISH PATH: `PR_REMEDIATE=0 make pr` remains the preferred route to GitHub — it runs
the Makefile checkers, then pushes and opens the PR. That preference is POLICY and is
unchanged. It is no longer enforced by denying execution: `git` and `gh` commands are
exempt from every governance gate (ops/autonomy/git_execution_exemption.py), so no deny
entry for them belongs here either. `make push` and the MCP create_pull_request/
push_files tools are still denied — they are not git/gh executables and the gate still
blocks them. This allow/deny split must agree with ops/autonomy/local_execution_gate.py,
and validate_claude_env.py fails when it does not, in both directions.
An allow entry here is what an agent reads as 'approved, no prompt', so git/gh forms the
workflow discourages are simply absent from both lists: permitted to execute, not
advertised as approved.
There is no standing autonomous-merge grant. merge_gate.py does not consult any
environment boolean; a flag set once in this configuration cannot authorize merge.
Merge is allowed only by a human per-session breakglass (L9_MERGE_AUTHORIZED) or a
scoped, expiring receipt that /l9-pr-remediation writes for the target repo (and PR).
Campaigns and make pr still do not merge, and only reach green + mergeable + resolved
threads, oldest first. Force pushes, hard resets, destructive cleanup, and admin-merge
remain forbidden by policy.
